tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Plan: Pink envelope → lilac gradient

## Context
The envelope is pure CSS. Every pink surface (back panel, side folds, front pocket) is built from two custom properties on `div.envelope`. The user wants a lilac gradient based on #E5BFD6, written in HSL.

#E5BFD6 converts to **hsl(324, 42%, 82%)**.

## Changes (only `css/style.css`)
1. Lines ~25-41, on `div.envelope`, replace the tint variables. They are bare H,S,L values consumed by `hsla(var(--tint), a)`, so nothing else needs to change.
   - `--tint: 338, 84%, 73%` → `324, 42%, 82%` (the target #E5BFD6, used as the gradient's darker stop)
   - `--tint-light: 337, 94%, 87%` → `324, 52%, 91%` (a lighter highlight of the same hue, so the existing top-to-bottom gradient stays visible)
2. Line 40, drop shadow: `hsla(333, 43%, 41%, 0.16)` → `hsla(324, 25%, 40%, 0.16)`. This keeps the shadow in the same lilac family instead of rose.
3. Leave the gradient rules on `.envelope-back`, `.fold-left`, `.fold-right` and `.fold-bottom` alone. They already use `--tint` and `--tint-light` and give the gradient.

## Notes
- The grain overlay (`body::after`) and the brown page background are untouched.
- #E5BFD6 is a dusty pinkish-lilac. If it looks too pink beside the brown background, the hue can be nudged toward 300° without touching the structure.

## Verification
- Open `index.html` in a browser (or use the `run` skill) and check the closed and lifted states.
- Confirm the back panel, both side folds and the front pocket show a smooth light-to-#E5BFD6 gradient.
- Confirm no pink (338° hue) remains: `grep -n "338\|337\|333" css/style.css` should return nothing relevant.

# Plan: Make the lilac envelope gradient bolder

## Context
The envelope was changed from pink to a lilac gradient based on #E5BFD6, which is `hsl(324, 42%, 82%)`. The user finds it lighter than expected and wants it bolder. The fix is to make the same hue deeper and more saturated.

The side folds and front pocket are semi-transparent (0.55-0.72 alpha) layers over the back panel, so they read lighter than the raw tint values. That is why the result looks paler than the numbers suggest.

## Changes (only `css/style.css`, lines 28-29)
Keep the hue at 324° so it is still the same lilac. Lower the lightness and raise the saturation:
- `--tint: 324, 42%, 82%` → `324, 50%, 70%` (the darker gradient stop, roughly #D58FBC)
- `--tint-light: 324, 52%, 91%` → `324, 56%, 82%` (the top highlight, which keeps a visible light-to-deep gradient)

Leave the drop shadow (`hsla(324, 25%, 40%, 0.16)`) and all gradient rules unchanged.

## Notes
- If it is still too light, lower lightness further (`--tint` to about 62%). If it turns too pink, shift the hue toward 310°.
- The grain overlay and the brown background are untouched.

## Verification
- Open `index.html` in a browser and check the closed and lifted states.
- Confirm the panel, side folds and pocket all show a clearly deeper lilac with a visible gradient.
- Confirm the cream letter and the postcard still stand out against the envelope.
